subject: Midterm expansion pricing and renewal anchoring
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Sanders <emma.sanders@aperturehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Midterm expansion pricing and renewal anchoring

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Aperture's usage spike this quarter is great to see — congrats to the team. Per our conversation, you mentioned a likely mid-contract expansion (approx. +45% token consumption on the current product) and interest in simplifying invoicing by co-terming the new commitment with your existing annual contract.

To move quickly and keep ProcOps happy, we sketched two feasible paths and attached a short proposal and a mutual action planner: Aperture_proposal_v2.pdf, MA_planner.xlsx. High level: 

1) Staged uplift (short-term top-up + co-term):
   - Immediate 3-month top-up of reserved units at a market uplift rate (we modeled ~12% uplift)
   - If you commit to convert top-up into a longer-term reserved bucket at renewal, we apply a blended invoice discount across remaining months to smooth billing

2) Instant annualize (co-term now):
   - Reprice remainder of the year to an annualized committed rate with a one-time credit offset to reflect midterm conversion
   - Requires PO + signoff from Procurement to lock in pricing and billing cadence

Questions for you so we can finalize numbers for legal/finance:
- Confirm estimated monthly token delta for Q3027028 (ballpark is fine)
- Which procurement cadence is Aperture targeting (PO now vs PO at renewal)?
- Any constraints on invoice splitting / cost-center mapping we should be aware of?

Next step: if you can share a short usage ramp table, Karthik and I will produce a compact pricing matrix (two scenarios + concession table) and run it by Finance for an approval path. Happy to schedule a 30-min alignment call later this week.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0198
Redwood Inference — Production-first inference for apps

Attachments: Aperture_proposal_v2.pdf (proposal summary), MA_planner.xlsx (mutual action planner)

From: Emma Sanders <emma.sanders@aperturehealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@aperturehealth.com, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Midterm expansion pricing and renewal anchoring

Hi Neha —

Appreciate the clear options. Quick answers:
- Estimated incremental tokens: we expect roughly +42–48% month-over-month versus current baseline for the next three months before leveling to +20% thereafter. I'll pull a short table from our usage dashboard and send it by EOD.
- Procurement preference: Procurement prefers a PO now for the top-up approach, but legal will only sign anything that doesn't materially change the annual budget line without CFO approval. So we'd need a split-invoice option or a credit structure that keeps year-over-year spend visibility.
- Cost-center mapping: finance requires separate invoice lines for the pilot BU vs enterprise BU — we can share a template.

Two asks from our side before we confirm a call: can Redwood provide a simple blended-rate example (per-1k-token) for each path and one example of how credits would amortize on the invoice? Also, any SLA implications for the higher throughput profile?

I'll attach the procurement contact separately if helpful. Thanks — Emma

Emma Sanders
VP, Product @ Aperture Health
emma.sanders@aperturehealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Sanders <emma.sanders@aperturehealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Midterm expansion pricing and renewal anchoring

Emma / Neha —

Thanks for the usage color, Emma — that's exactly what we needed. I put together a compact pricing matrix (attached pricing_matrix.csv) with the blended-rate examples and an amortization sketch for credits. Highlights below: 

- Option A (Staged uplift + co-term conversion):
  • 3-month top-up at a short-term uplift of 12% over current per-1k-token list rate
  • If Aperture converts top-up to a committed annual bucket at renewal, we apply a retrospective blended credit that effectively reduces the remaining months' per-1k rate by ~9% (net blended uplift over the full period ~3%)
  • Invoices: we can split lines so Procurement sees the top-up separately and Finance sees the blended adjustment at renewal (credit memo).

- Option B (Immediate annualize / co-term now):
  • Annualize the incremental commitment now at a 10% discount to current list per-1k (requires PO + legal signoff)
  • Redwood issues a one-time conversion credit to smooth the year-over-year visibility for Aperture's CFO (we model the credit on realized usage vs committed)

SLA: no SLA change required for either path; we have headroom in the serving pool and can preserve latency SLOs with our dedicated routing. If Aperture wants capacity guarantees above current committed throughput we can add a service-level buffer with a small premium (listed in matrix).

Next steps I propose:
- Neha: lock a 30-min alignment call Thursday 10–10:30 PT with Emma + Procurement contact
- I will run the attached pricing_matrix.csv by Finance for a quick approval path and share any gating questions

Karthik
Head of Renewals | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com | +1 650-555-0123

Attachments: pricing_matrix.csv (blended examples + amortization)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Sanders <emma.sanders@aperturehealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Midterm expansion pricing and renewal anchoring

Emma —

Adding quick procurement checklist so your team can share with Legal/Finance: 
- PO or SOW: define whether this is a short-term PO (3 months) or amendment to annual SOW
- Invoice split: indicate cost-center codes for pilot vs enterprise lines (we can map to two invoice line items)
- Credit mechanics: credit applied at the time of annual conversion as a credit memo against the renewal invoice; we amortize over remaining months unless you prefer a lump-sum 
- SLA buffer: optional dedicated capacity buffer if you want throughput headroom guaranteed; 2%-5% premium depending on size

If you send the usage table (Emma) we'll finalize the numbers and mark the document as "Procurement-ready". Happy to join the call if helpful.

Best,
Jonas Weber
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: none
